title: Akamai launches managed inference and isolated agent execution
dek: New managed services pair model serving with runtime containment for autonomous agents at the edge.
evidence: Akamai vendor announcement; no independent latency or security assessment supplied
takeaway: Test sandbox escape resistance, filesystem and network policy, cold starts and observability before adopting an agent runtime.

sections.title: Architecture

bullets.detail: Akamai Inference provides managed model-serving capacity; Akamai Agent Sandbox provides isolated execution boundaries for agents using tools and data.
Akamai positions deployment across its distributed cloud to reduce proximity to applications/data while retaining controlled execution.

paragraphs: Two layers: Akamai Inference provides managed model-serving capacity; Akamai Agent Sandbox provides isolated execution boundaries for agents using tools and data.
Placement: Akamai positions deployment across its distributed cloud to reduce proximity to applications/data while retaining controlled execution.

sections.title: Evaluation

bullets.detail: Sandboxing reduces host blast radius but does not by itself validate tool authorization, data exfiltration policies or model prompt-injection resistance.
Compare p50/p95 tool latency, cold-start cost, network egress enforcement, resource limits, tenant separation and incident logging to a self-hosted baseline.

paragraphs: Security boundary: Sandboxing reduces host blast radius but does not by itself validate tool authorization, data exfiltration policies or model prompt-injection resistance.
